The '''Tusil River''' is the eastern of the two great rivers systems that define [[Alzuria (region)]], the other being the _______  . The river flows south from the [[Untschalle]] through the [[Taiylsh Desert]] , before merging with the [[Vixon|Vixon River]] and reaching to the [[Tasa Bay]].

The Tusil passes through historical cities like [[Zandrek]], [[Dergavat]], [[Veshgadar]], and [[Dy]]. It is also home to archaeological sites and ancient religious communities, including the _________ , who use it for baptism. In ancient times, the Tusil nurtured the [[Kaaldari Empire]].

Today, the Tusil faces modern threats from geopolitical instability, [[wikipedia:Dam|dam]] projects, poor water management, and [[wikipedia:Climate_change|climate change]], leading to concerns about its sustainability. Efforts to protect and preserve the river's legacy are ongoing, with local [[wikipedia:Archaeology|archaeologists]] and activists working to safeguard its future.

==Etymology==
From [[Ukhdari Language|Ukhdari]] Tusil, from [[Ancient Kaalsite Language|Ancient Kaalsite]] (Tosal), an alternative form of  (Tysil), from Old [[Aiisaran Language|Aiisaran]].

The [[Ancient Kaalsite Language|Ancient Kaalsite]] form Tosal probably derived from "running water"). The [[Unwosian Language|Unwosian]] term, which can be interpreted as "the fast river", contrasts the Tusil to its neighbour, the [[Vixon Rver]] , whose leisurely pace caused it to deposit more silt and build up a higher bed than the Tusil. The Unwosian form was borrowed into Kaalsite and from there into the other Alzurian languages 

In [[Southern Alzurian languages]], it is known as Vossol, "the Great Water".
[[File:Tigris River in early morning.jpg|thumb|500x500px|<bdi>The Tusil river is in the early morning.</bdi>]]

==Geography==
The Tusil is around 3500km (2174 mi) long. The river originates from [[Lake Arnite]], then flows through 400km (248mi) through Estijan and Ikzen before forming part of the Ikzen-Urbiqu border. 

Close to its confluence with the [[Vixon River|Vixon]], the Tusil splits into several channels. The artificial [[Ziala a-Xia canal|Ziala a-Xia]] branches off from Szomedin, to join Vixon near [[Zarhesh]]. Further downstream, two other [[wikipedia:Distributary|distributary channels]] branch off to feed the [[Haqla Marshes]]. The main channel continues southwards, that drains into the [[Laiqaan Marshes]]. According to Pala and other ancient historians, the Vixon originally had its outlet into the sea combaiend from that of the Tusil.

[[Veshagdar]], the old capital of Alzuria, stands on the banks of the Tusil. The port city of [[Dy]] straddles the [[Tasa Bay]]. In ancient times, many of the great cities of Alzuria stood on or near the Tusil, drawing water from it to [[wikipedia:Irrigation|irrigate]] the civilization of the Ukhdari. Notable Tusil-side cities included [[Fereste]], [[Aphia]], and [[Dy]], while the city of Lagash was irrigated by the Tusil via a canal dug around 2700 B.F.A 
==Navigation==
The Tusil has long been an important transport route in a largely desert country. Shallow-draft vessels can go as far as [[Zandrek]], but rafts have historically been needed for transport downstream from [[Vashkiri]].
==Management and water quality==
The Tusil is starting to be dammed in [[Ealdorii]] to provide water for irrigating the arid and semi-desert regions bordering the river valley. Damming has also been important for averting floods in [[Alzuria (region)]], to which the Tusil has historically been notoriously prone following April melting of snow in the [[Untschalle]]. [[Zarshird Dam]] is the largest dam in Ealdorii.

Recent [[Ukhdari]] damming of the rivers' tributaries has been the subject of some controversy, for both its environmental effects within [[Ukhdari]] and its potential to reduce the flow of water downstream.

Water from both parts of the river is used as a means of pressure during conflicts.

In 1753 a major breakthrough in developing consensus between multiple stakeholder representatives of Ealdorii and Ukhdari on a Plan of Action for promoting exchange and calibration of data and standards pertaining to Tusil river flows was achieved. The consensus, known as the "Zarshird Consensus On Tusil River".
